summary: Internal roadmap / launch readiness meeting. Main focus: incident review from 2026-12-08 (KV cache invalidation during canary), adjustments to rollout and autoscaling policies, benchmark checklist for final launch, and ownership of postmortem and fixes. Agreed to freeze non-critical changes, run expanded benchmarks, and tighten canary/rollback criteria.
topics: Incident recap: KV cache invalidation on canary rollout
Rollout policy changes: canary size, rollback thresholds
Benchmarks: 500 concurrent clients, end-to-end latency distribution
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Okay folks, let's get started. Thanks for joining — we've got an hour, maybe a bit more, for roadmap and the incident review. Marcus, can you kick off with a quick recap of the outage last week?
[00:18] Marcus: Yeah, sure. Uh, quick recap — on 2026-12-08 during the canary for the new quantized transformer we saw a KV cache invalidation that caused elevated tail latency. It was essentially a race between cache eviction and secondary lookups, so a subset of requests re-serialized and then hit hot paths.
[00:36] Marcus: The sequence was: deploy, small canary 5%, then after ~10 minutes error rate climbed, we saw p50 okay but p95/p99 spiking, memory thrash on two nodes, and auto-replace kicked in which made it worse.
[00:50] Priya: And to add, auto-scaler reacted to CPU pressure and spun up extra nodes but they joined with a cold KV cache, so the effective load on origin nodes changed. The handoff was messy — we'd expected graceful warming but the new nodes were asked to serve immediately.
[01:10] Sofia: Right, so the main failure modes were race in cache invalidation and misconfigured autoscale cooldowns?
[01:20] Priya: Exactly. Also some of the canary routing rules allowed traffic to the new shard before the full prefix warming completed.
[01:30] Liam: Can we quantify how often the invalidation happened? Is this a 1/1000 request thing or bigger?
[01:38] Marcus: Preliminary logs show around 0.8% of requests hitting the invalidation path in the canary window, but those accounted for most tail spikes because each one serialized more work.
[01:48] Ava: From a UX/product perspective, the user-visible latency was intermittent which is worse than consistent slowness — a lot of perceived instability. That hurts trust more.
[02:00] Diego: There's also a configuration mismatch between the runtime's cache TTL and the orchestration hooks. We didn't coordinate the warmup window in the helm chart with the runtime's readiness probe.
[02:12] Marcus: Yeah, the readiness probe declared ready once process up, not once KV warm. We need a KV-warm readiness check.
[02:22] Priya: I'm thinking add a pre-warm step and then gate traffic with a gradual ramp config — like 1% -> 5% -> 25% over X minutes but only after KV warm confirmed.
[02:36] Sofia: Ok, action item — Priya to draft a gating proposal. Liam will own rollout doc updates.
[02:44] Liam: Yep, I'll add canary ramp and explicit rollback thresholds, plus a 'no-autoscale for first Y minutes' option for canaries so we don't create cold nodes too early.
[02:58] Marcus: On the runtime side we'll add a KV-initialized readiness probe and a circuit-breaker for serialization path. Also add telemetry to count invalidations.
[03:10] Ava: Quick question — are these changes going to delay launch? Our marketing timeline is tight.
[03:17] Sofia: We discussed options — our preference is to keep date but enforce a hard freeze on non-critical changes and expand the bench window. If benchmarks pass with the fixes, we go. If not, we postpone by one week.
[03:32] Marcus: Bench plan: run 500 concurrent clients end-to-end hitting real prompts, include cold-start scenarios, and measure p50/p95/p99, plus throughput. I'll run with quantized and dequantized variants.
[03:45] Diego: I'll instrument request fanout and cache hit ratios so we can correlate.
[03:52] Priya: Also capture node join/leave timings and autoscaler decisions. The autoscaler logs are messy today. We should export to a dedicated dashboard.
[04:05] Liam: Who's owning the dashboard?
[04:07] Diego: I'll spin up a dashboard in Grafana, link it in the launchdoc.
[04:11] Sofia: Good. Next, the incident postmortem — Priya?
[04:14] Priya: I'm drafting it. High level: root cause is KV invalidation race coupled with autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration. Contributing factors: readiness probe mismatch, lack of canary gating, insufficient telemetry. Action items we'll enumerate. Draft ready by 2026-12-16 for review.
[04:30] Marcus: One note on telemetry — some of the KV events were logged as generic errors, so we missed them in alerting. We should add specific metric for 'kv_invalidation_count' and alert when >0.1% sustained.
[04:45] Priya: Agreed, alert threshold will be conservative for canaries but we need early warning.
[04:52] Sofia: Let's talk launch checklist items — freeze window?
[04:55] Liam: Propose freeze starting 48 hours before the ship window. Only critical fixes allowed after that, with SE/PM sign-off.
[05:03] Ava: Design will also freeze assets 24 hours out; we can plan contingency messaging.
[05:09] Sofia: Ok. On canary size: we had 5% previously. Should we reduce to 2% then ramp to 10%?
[05:16] Marcus: I like 2% initial, but longer observation window. The issue happened within 10 minutes — we should watch for at least 30 minutes at each stage.
[05:25] Liam: That will impact time to ship but it's safer. Build into L0 timeline.
[05:31] Sofia: Competitor note — Anthropic just announced an auto-warm feature in their runtime, so we need parity for customers who worry about cold starts. Not a blocker but worth noting.
[05:43] Diego: On hardware, the quantized model runs with lower memory footprint but higher serialization CPU. That explains why CPU pressure triggered autoscaler. We might tune burst capacity to absorb initial spike.
[05:56] Marcus: There's also an option to pre-allocate a small warm pool for canaries (dedicated warm nodes) which don't auto-scale immediately; it costs more but improves stability.
[06:06] Priya: Let's add cost-vs-stability tradeoffs to the launch doc.
[06:10] Sofia: Agree. Next, risk register items — add 'KV invalidation during canary', 'Autoscale cold join', 'Telemetry gaps', 'Rollback test not executed'.
[06:24] Marcus: About rollback tests — we didn't exercise them in staging fully. We should run a forced rollback in the staging canary and validate no residual cache issues.
[06:34] Diego: Note: the rollback path needs to ensure old cache is rebuilt or traffic is drained correctly. We'll script graceful drain.
[06:42] Sofia: Ok, let's go through the checklist quickly: readiness probes (Diego/Marcus), gating config (Priya/Liam), telemetry & dashboards (Diego/Priya), bench plan (Marcus), postmortem (Priya), launch freeze (Sofia).
[06:58] Marcus: For the benchmark I'll use our standard prompts list + a synthetic high-concurrency suite. Expect results by 2026-12-18.
[07:06] Ava: I'll prepare fallback UX messaging in case of partial rollbacks.
[07:12] Sofia: Anything else?
[07:15] Liam: One more ops ask — add a temporary 'no-auto-scaling' label for canary pods so we can opt out quickly.
[07:22] Priya: We'll test that in staging.
[07:25] Marcus: Also, small note: rename 'KV cache' metric to 'kv_cache' in logs — sometimes it appears as 'k v cache' and breaks parsers, small but annoying.
[07:36] Sofia: Good catch.
[07:38] Speaker 7: Quick side note, legal flagged SOC 2 wording in the launch collateral, ask PM to sync with compliance.
[07:46] Sofia: I'll loop in compliance. Noted.
[07:50] Priya: I'll share the incident logs link and a short tl;dr after this meeting.
[07:55] Sofia: Great. Recap of next steps: Priya postmortem by 12/16, Marcus bench by 12/18, Diego dashboard & telemetry by 12/17, Liam rollout doc by 12/16, Sofia freeze announcement by 12/17. Any objections?
[08:18] Diego: None.
[08:19] Ava: No.
[08:20] Liam: All good.
[08:22] Sofia: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene if the postmortem surfaces anything urgent; otherwise next sync is the pre-launch readiness meeting on 2026-12-20. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-heard acronyms ("k v cache", "sock two" for SOC 2) and some run-on sentences typical of automated transcripts. Links shared: incident-logs-20261208 (internal link), launchdoc-v3 (internal link), bench-results-template (internal link).
